solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Home ground

parts.note: read literally, the earth of the place one calls home, the land where one was born

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sports team's own pitch, where it plays its home matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting sense of a team's home stadium is the decoy; the phrase is read as the soil of one's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the country of one's birth, the land one belongs to by origin.

clue.text: He didn't save a single animal from drowning

definitions.text: He didn't save a single animal from drowning

parts.words: He didn't save a single animal from drowning
parts.note: the ark-builder of Genesis took the animals two by two, so none was single

explanation.surface: Sounds like a callous man who let every animal drown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical patriarch saved animals in pairs from the Flood, so none went aboard alone.

clue.text: Wonders if there will be an increase in those commuting

indicators.note: commuting in the sense of exchanging places, so the letters swap around

parts.note: a rise is an increase
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muses whether the number of commuters will go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the rise among the letters of THOSE, all mixed by 'commuting'.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate or hypothesise about something is to wonder about it.

clue.text: Drug containers European holds one up to get

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
holds says the European contains the numeral

parts.note: a Slav is a European from the east of the continent
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A European holds up a drug container.
explanation.definitionFit: Small glass bottles for medicine are the containers for doses of a drug.

clue.text: Contends vehicle reversed onto main road a little way over

indicators.note: reversed turns the vehicle round, backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI

indicators.note: over means the little road is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: St is short for street, a little way or road

explanation.surface: A driver reverses onto a main road and goes a little way.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway north from London, and the setter writes the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit that something is so is to contend or argue it, as a lawyer does.

clue.text: Where schoolchildren are when teacher does

definitions.text: Where schoolchildren are when teacher does

parts.words: Where schoolchildren are when teacher does
parts.note: split 2,5 it says where they are, and as one word what the teacher does

explanation.surface: A riddle about the classroom: what links pupils' places and the teacher's action?
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as IN FORMS for the pupils; whole, it is the teacher telling them things.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher tells or instructs, passing on knowledge; a form is a British school class.

clue.text: Invite me to cover story

indicators.note: the two words Invite me cover, or hold within them, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be invited along to report on a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item is a single story or report in a paper or broadcast.

clue.text: For the illiterate, it's not a flaw

definitions.meaning: the dialect contraction '... stands for it is not

explanation.surface: A pedant insists that speaking ungrammatically is no fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish or trace of corruption mars something, as a defect does.

clue.text: Voicing of surprise at the compiler's excellence

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of astonishment, like gosh
the setter speaks of herself as me, so her virtue is my virtue

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in amazement at how good the setter is.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter refers to themselves as 'me', so 'the compiler's' gives MY.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment; goodness also means virtue, the second reading.

clue.text: What the Colosseum was a long while back

indicators.note: back means the letters of the phrase for a long while are read from end to start

parts.note: the indefinite article in its form an
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A history quiz question: what was the Colosseum a long time ago?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a long while' is AN ERA, and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum was an amphitheatre, a venue where gladiators fought before spectators.

clue.text: Happening to step on a banana skin, you might …?

definitions.meaning: occurring, as in what is happening to someone

definitions.text: to step on a banana skin, you might …?
definitions.meaning: the sentence is completed by the phrase ..., split 2,7

explanation.surface: A slapstick scene: tread on a banana skin and you know what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a fill-in-the-blank: split the answer as BE FALLING to finish the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something befalling a person is happening to them, usually something unwelcome.

clue.text: Without switch, this light can go out. Magic?

definitions.text: Without switch, this light can go out. Magic?

parts.words: Without switch, this light can go out. Magic?
parts.note: an old oil or candle light has no switch and can blow out; preceded by Magic it names an early slide projector

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer sees a light with no switch go out, and wonders if it is magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-electric lamp in a glass case, and with Magic before it, an early image projector.

clue.text: Tries playing football first, more in need of training

indicators.note: first puts the football letters ahead of the rearranged word

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a form of football

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of Tries are put into play in a new order

explanation.surface: A rugby player who tries playing football first is out of practice for his main sport.
explanation.walkthrough: RU stands for rugby union; 'Tries' is scored in rugby, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusty skill has weakened through lack of use, so it needs practice or training again.

clue.text: I couldn't agree less

parts.note: a play on I couldn't agree more: the opposite is a flat denial, the retort to a claim

explanation.surface: A twist on the stock phrase of complete agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt rejoinder of contradiction, saying that a claim is false rather than true.

clue.text: ____ shows how fast phoney bullet travels

definitions.meaning: the line in the clue is itself a gap left for writing in
a blank is a dummy cartridge, and its pace its speed

explanation.surface: A puzzle with a gap that supposedly reveals the speed of a dummy round.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens with a gap that is the first definition; split the answer as BLANK'S PACE for the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The empty line printed in the clue is an unfilled gap, exactly an empty area for writing.

clue.text: Hears close to wall is high nest

indicators.note: close to means the final letter, the end, of the word wall

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: high in the sense of intoxicated, so the letters of nest are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone presses an ear to the wall beside a bird's nest perched up high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like it describes the nest, but it signals the jumble of NEST into TENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear something attentively is to listen to it; the verbs are close synonyms.

clue.text: Figure American in green rigged to blow up

indicators.note: in puts the figure and the American inside the rearranged green
rigged means arranged dishonestly, so green's letters are reordered

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An American figure in a rigged green outfit ready to explode.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger, a magnifying sense.

clue.text: Marching orders given to child — somebody else's

definitions.text: Marching orders given to child — somebody else's

indicators.note: given to says the marching word is joined to the boy

parts.note: a step, such as the goose step, is a marching gait called out on parade
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A parent barks marching orders at a child that isn't theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somebody else's' points to the whole picture: a child who is your partner's, not your own.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner's boy from an earlier marriage is someone else's child, related only by marriage.

clue.text: Say 'Consume meal ordered: end of argument'

indicators.note: consume means the word for say swallows the other letters

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of meal are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone says eat the meal you ordered, and that's the end of the argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock in which neither side can win, as in chess, ends a dispute without a victor.

clue.text: Sleet beating into window frame disregarded, was cosy

indicators.note: into places the stirred-up sleet inside what is left of window
the frame of window is its outer letters, two at each end, and these are ignored
sleet beating against glass is driven about, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Sleet lashes the window while someone ignores it, warm and snug inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame disregarded' strips WI and OW from window, leaving ND; 'beating' turns SLEET into ESTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have snuggled down comfortably is to have been snug and warm, the past tense of a cosy settling.

clue.text: Weaken and cross out 'seizing power'

indicators.note: seizing means the word for cross out grabs the power letter inside it

parts.note: to delete is to strike out
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Instructions to weaken a document and strike out the phrase about taking control.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain or use up resources is to reduce them, so to exhaust or weaken.

clue.text: You and I recalled sandy frolics and leisure time, perhaps

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the pronoun is reversed

parts.note: you and I together are us

indicators.note: frolics suggests the letters of sandy romping into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people remember playing on the beach in their spare time.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekend days off are an example of free time, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: In private, for instance, recognitions of inferiority

definitions.text: In private, for instance, recognitions of inferiority

parts.words: In private, for instance, recognitions of inferiority
parts.note: a private soldier gives these gestures to an officer, acknowledging lower rank

explanation.surface: Sounds like confessing one's inadequacies privately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' is the soldier of lowest rank, not secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier's raised hand to a superior acknowledges their senior rank.

clue.text: Interrupt French fantasies for retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the French word runs backwards

parts.note: reves are dreams or fantasies in French

explanation.surface: Someone breaks off their French daydreams about stopping work.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off or break a connection is to interrupt it, as in severing communications.

clue.text: By quarter past five, urges us to flee separately to make border

indicators.note: past means the quarter comes after the five

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
E, east, is a quarter of the compass

indicators.note: the two letters of us leave the word urges separately, not side by side

explanation.surface: By a quarter past five, someone urges us to run off in different directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter past five' looks like a time; it is E after V.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge or brink of something, such as a grass verge beside a road, is its border.

clue.text: Punishable offence by men in time of easy contraception

definitions.meaning: plundering is a crime committed by soldiers
split 4,3 as ..., the era of the contraceptive pill

explanation.surface: A claim that men's crimes flourished once contraception became easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PILL AGE for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Plundering and looting, typically by troops in war, has long been a crime.

clue.text: Gather from fool's confession

definitions.meaning: split 2,3, a fool might admit I am an ass

explanation.surface: A fool gathers to make a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or collect a large amount is to gather it up.

clue.text: Well-groomed, carrying a bag

indicators.note: carrying means the bag holds the letter inside

parts.note: a net is a mesh bag, as for shopping or fish

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed person carrying a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and trim in appearance, the sense of a smart, well-turned-out person.

clue.text: Negotiator takes mere flip through contract

indicators.note: takes says the negotiator holds the other letters
through says these letters pass right into the middle

parts.note: an agent negotiates on a client's behalf

indicators.note: flip in the sense of flipping out, going wild, so the letters of mere are jumbled

explanation.surface: A deal-maker merely flicks through a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding deal, an accord between parties.

clue.text: Saying 'Gadzooks!', ace relapses

indicators.note: relapses suggests falling back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: egad is another old-fashioned oath like gadzooks
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims an old oath and an ace slips back.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb or maxim is a traditional saying, like an old adage.

clue.text: For most of the race, neck and neck

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: a race is an event in athletics

explanation.surface: Two runners are level for most of the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck and neck means level with each other, tied, with neither ahead.

clue.text: Going on and on about, resist exploding 'Shut up!'

indicators.note: about says the word for shut up goes round the other letters

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut up or confined

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters of resist apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to be quiet bursts out resisting, going on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' looks like a command; it is PENT, confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that continues relentlessly without stopping is unremitting or continuing.
